messages.subject: filtered input into a dataframe
parts:

Suppose I have 2 pairs of vairables. In each pair, the first is a
control for the other one.

I want to input only the target variable inside a data frame based on
his control variable.

for illustration:

data<-data.frame (Var2 (where Ctrl1==1), Var2 (where Ctrl2==1))

How do I do that?
Thnx

messages.author: b24c10731fdfceaf
messages.subject: Re: [Israel RUG] Re: filtered input into a dataframe
parts:
A simple example:

set.seed(4)
a1 = data.frame(ctrl1 = sample(letters[1:5]), var1 = rnorm(5))
a2 = data.frame(ctrl1 = sample(letters[1:5]), var2 = rnorm(5))
merge(a1,a2, by = "ctrl1")

messages.author: b24c10731fdfceaf
messages.subject: Re: [Israel RUG] Re: filtered input into a dataframe
parts:
ok,
in this case, what you want is to take your original data.frame, and start having conditions on it.

For example:
let's say the data.frame name is xx.

ss <- xx$V41 == 0 & V43 ==0
xx[ss,]

But now, if you also want only the even V42 V44, then you'd want:
ss <- xx$V41 == 0 & xx$V43 ==0  &  xx$V42%%2 ==0   &  xx$V42%%2 ==0
xx[ss,]

messages.subject: Re: [Israel RUG] Re: filtered input into a dataframe
parts:
Assaf-
The output of what you want will not fit into a single data frame since each output variable will have a different length. 
Unless there is a MASSIVE amount of variable, I would try extracting and subsetting  each pair of control-value manually.

For the first pair it would look like:
data$V42[ data$V41==0 ]

This process could be automated if there are many such pairs, but as I said- since each pair returns a different length, there is not point of doing it simultaneously.

J

On Thu, Nov 11, 2010 at 11:55 AM, Tal Galili <tal.g...@gmail.com> wrote:
You can check these things by using a question mark on them.
?"%%"
Will show you that it is a modulo operator (you wanted the even numbers).
& is the AND operator.

Tal

On Thu, Nov 11, 2010 at 11:02 AM, Tal Galili <tal.g...@gmail.com> wrote:
ok,
in this case, what you want is to take your original data.frame, and start having conditions on it.

For example:
let's say the data.frame name is xx.

ss <- xx$V41 == 0 & V43 ==0
xx[ss,]

But now, if you also want only the even V42 V44, then you'd want:
ss <- xx$V41 == 0 & xx$V43 ==0  &  xx$V42%%2 ==0   &  xx$V42%%2 ==0
xx[ss,]
